description: The Tabular data-frame framework introduced in Version 14.2: constructing and converting Tabular objects, column and row objects, schema and structure inspection, column typing, renaming/inserting/deleting/transforming/constructing columns, row aggregation and grouping, pivoting between long and wide layouts and pivot tables, and the columnwise-evaluation helpers. Only functions confirmed on reference.wolfram.com or in the product's usage messages are listed; Tabular itself is catalogued in the datasets chunk.

tools.name: ToTabular
tools.description: Converts data (list of rows or associations, matrix, Dataset, TimeSeries/TemporalData, SparseArray, spatial/graph data) into a Tabular object, optionally specifying the structure form ("Rows", "Columns", "Matrix", "Associations"...) and conversion directives such as column keys; the general entry point when data is not already rectangular rows. Import of CSV, TSV, XLSX and Parquet files returns Tabular objects directly in 14.2+, so ToTabular is mainly for in-memory data.
tools.usage:
ToTabular[data]
ToTabular[data, form]
ToTabular[data, form, <|"ColumnKeys" -> {...}, ...|>]
ToTabular[matrix, "Matrix"]
ToTabular[timeSeries]
ToTabular[dataset]

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Rows, columns, matrix, associations, Dataset, TimeSeries etc.

tools.notes: Introduced in 14.2. FromTabular converts back to other structures.

tools.name: FromTabular
tools.description: Converts a Tabular object to another structure: "Rows" (list of lists), "Columns", "Matrix", "Associations" (list of row associations), "Dataset", "TimeSeries", "EventSeries", "TemporalData", with an optional directives association (e.g. which column holds times). Normal[tab] is the shortcut for the row-association form.
tools.usage:
FromTabular[tab, "Rows"]
FromTabular[tab, "Matrix"]
FromTabular[tab, "Dataset"]
FromTabular[tab, "TimeSeries", <|"TimeColumn" -> "date"|>]
Normal[tab]

tools.name: TabularQ
tools.description: Tests whether an expression is a valid Tabular object, for argument validation in functions that accept either Tabular or Dataset input.
tools.usage: TabularQ[expr]

tools.name: TabularColumn
tools.description: TabularColumn[{v1, v2, ...}] creates a typed column vector with an efficiently stored element type detected automatically (numeric, string, date, quantity, entity, categorical, with a validity bitmap for missing values), or with an explicit element type and conversion method; columns extracted from a Tabular (tab[All, "col"]) are of this form. Use it to build Tabular objects column by column or to force a type.
tools.usage:
TabularColumn[{v1, v2, ...}]
TabularColumn[{v1, ...}, etype]
TabularColumn[{v1, ...}, etype, method]
tab[All, "col"] (* a TabularColumn *)
tools.example:
col = TabularColumn[{1, 2, Missing[], 4}, "Integer64"]
Tabular[<|"id" -> col, "name" -> TabularColumn[{"a", "b", "c", "d"}]|>]

tools.name: TabularRow
tools.description: Represents a single row of a Tabular object (as returned by tab[i] or by row-wise Map), carrying the column keys so that fields are accessed as row["col"] or #col inside functions; TabularRow[{v1, v2, ...}, {key1, key2, ...}] builds one explicitly. It is the row analogue of TabularColumn.
tools.usage:
TabularRow[{v1, v2, ...}]
TabularRow[{v1, v2, ...}, {key1, key2, ...}]
tab[i] (* a TabularRow *)
row["col"]
Normal[row] (* association *)

tools.name: TabularStructure
tools.description: Reports column-level metadata of a Tabular: element type, number of missing values, distinct-value counts and other properties for all or selected columns and properties - the equivalent of pandas info()/describe() for checking data quality and types after import.
tools.usage:
TabularStructure[tab]
TabularStructure[tab, {"col1", "col2"}]
TabularStructure[tab, All, {"ColumnType", "MissingCount"}]

tools.name: TabularSchema
tools.description: Represents the schema (column keys and element types, plus row-key and other properties) of a Tabular; TabularSchema[tab] extracts it, and TabularSchema[schema, "prop" -> val] modifies properties so the schema can be applied to new data with Tabular[data, schema] for consistent typing across files. ColumnKeys and ColumnTypes are the quick accessors.
tools.usage:
TabularSchema[tab]
TabularSchema[schema, "prop" -> val]
TabularSchema[schema, <|"prop1" -> val1, ...|>]
Tabular[data, schema]
tools.example:
schema = TabularSchema[Import["jan.csv"]];
feb = Tabular[Import["feb.csv", "Rows"] // Rest, schema] (* same column types *)

tools.name: ColumnTypes
tools.description: Gives the element types of all or selected columns of a Tabular (e.g. "Integer64", "Real64", "String", "Date", "Categorical"), and ColumnKeys the column names (optionally matching a string pattern or predicate); ColumnKeyExistsQ tests for a column. Use them for schema checks before transformations.
tools.usage:
ColumnTypes[tab]
ColumnTypes[tab, {"col1", "col2"}]
ColumnKeys[tab]
ColumnKeys[tab, "patt"]
ColumnKeys[tab, crit]
ColumnKeyExistsQ[tab, "col"]
ColumnKeyExistsQ["col"][tab]

tools.name: CastColumns
tools.description: Changes the element type of specified columns of a Tabular (string to number, number to categorical, text to date, ...), converting values and marking failures as missing - the explicit type-conversion step after importing text data or before machine learning.
tools.usage:
CastColumns[tab, "col" -> "Real64"]
CastColumns[tab, {"col1" -> "Integer64", "col2" -> "Date"}]
CastColumns[tab, "col" -> "Categorical"]

parameters.name: col -> type
parameters.description: Column key and target element type.

tools.name: RenameColumns
tools.description: Renames columns of a Tabular by rules (old -> new) or by position with a list of new names, with an operator form for pipelines; used to normalise imported headers and avoid key conflicts before joins.
tools.usage:
RenameColumns[tab, {"old1" -> "new1", "old2" -> "new2"}]
RenameColumns[tab, {"new1", "new2", ...}]
RenameColumns[renamings][tab]
tools.example:
tab // RenameColumns[{"Unit Price" -> "price", "Qty" -> "quantity"}]
RenameColumns[tab, ToLowerCase /@ ColumnKeys[tab]]

tools.name: InsertColumns
tools.description: Inserts new columns with given values (lists, TabularColumns or constants) into a Tabular, appended at the end or after specified anchor columns, with an operator form; use TransformColumns when the new column is computed from existing rows.
tools.usage:
InsertColumns[tab, {"col" -> values}]
InsertColumns[tab, {"col1" -> vals1, "col2" -> vals2}]
InsertColumns[tab, {"col" -> values}, "after"]
InsertColumns[cspec][tab]

parameters.name: col -> values
parameters.description: New column key and its values (length = number of rows) or a constant.

tools.name: DeleteColumns
tools.description: Deletes the specified columns (keys, patterns or a predicate on keys) from a Tabular, with an operator form; the complement of ConstructColumns for keeping only some columns.
tools.usage:
DeleteColumns[tab, "col"]
DeleteColumns[tab, {"col1", "col2"}]
DeleteColumns[cols][tab]

tools.name: TransformColumns
tools.description: Adds (or overwrites) columns computed by applying a function to each row, with #col slot access to existing columns and successive application of several rules; operator form for pipelines. Wrap sub-expressions in ColumnwiseValue for whole-column computations (e.g. subtracting the column mean) inside the row function.
tools.usage:
TransformColumns[tab, "ncol" -> f]
TransformColumns[tab, {"ncol1" -> f1, "ncol2" -> f2}]
TransformColumns[tab, "total" -> (#price #qty &)]
TransformColumns[tab, "z" -> ((#x - ColumnwiseValue[Mean[#x]])/ColumnwiseValue[StandardDeviation[#x]] &)]
TransformColumns[transfs][tab]

parameters.name: ncol -> f
parameters.description: New/overwritten column key and a function of the row (slots #col).

tools.name: ConstructColumns
tools.description: Returns a new Tabular containing only the specified existing columns, or new columns constructed by functions of each row (like SELECT expr AS name in SQL) - the projection operation; TransformColumns keeps existing columns while adding, ConstructColumns keeps only what is listed.
tools.usage:
ConstructColumns[tab, {"col1", "col2"}]
ConstructColumns[tab, {"ncol1" -> f1, "ncol2" -> f2}]
ConstructColumns[tab, {"name", "total" -> (#price #qty &)}]
ConstructColumns[cspec][tab]

tools.name: AggregateRows
tools.description: Reduces a Tabular to aggregates: AggregateRows[tab, {"key" -> f, ...}] applies aggregation functions to the whole table (f receives the columns as #col), and AggregateRows[tab, fspec, gspec] groups rows by the distinct values of one or more columns (or a function) before aggregating - the GROUP BY of Tabular; operator forms exist for both.
tools.usage:
AggregateRows[tab, {"total" -> Total[#amount] &, "n" -> Length}]
AggregateRows[tab, {"mean" -> Mean[#value] &}, "group"]
AggregateRows[tab, {"mean" -> Mean[#value] &}, {"g1", "g2"}]
AggregateRows[tab, fspec, DateValue[#date, "Month"] &]
AggregateRows[fspec, gspec][tab]

parameters.name: fspec
parameters.description: Rules key -> aggregation function of the (sub)table columns.

parameters.name: gspec
parameters.description: Column key(s) or function defining the groups.

tools.example:
byRegion = AggregateRows[sales, {"revenue" -> Total[#price #qty] &, "orders" -> Length}, "region"]
AggregateRows[sales, {"avg" -> Mean[#price] &}, {"region", "year"}]

tools.name: PivotToColumns
tools.description: Pivots a long table to wide form: the distinct values of a variable column become new column keys and a value column supplies their values (several value columns allowed), i.e. the inverse of PivotFromColumns (melt/unpivot); PivotTable builds classic cross-tabulations with an aggregation function over row and column keys.
tools.usage:
PivotToColumns[tab, "varcol" -> "valcol"]
PivotToColumns[tab, "varcol" -> {"val1", "val2"}]
PivotToColumns[tab, {rule1, rule2}]
PivotTable[tab, "rowkey", "colkey", f]
PivotTable[tab, "rowkey", "colkey", {"sum" -> Total[#amount] &}]

parameters.name: varcol
parameters.description: Column whose values become new column keys.

tools.name: PivotFromColumns
tools.description: Pivots a wide table to long (tidy) form: the listed columns are replaced by two columns - one holding the former column names (variables) and one holding their values - so that several measurement columns can be grouped, plotted or aggregated uniformly; the inverse of PivotToColumns.
tools.usage:
PivotFromColumns[tab, {"col1", "col2", ...} -> {"variable", "value"}]
PivotFromColumns[tab, {prule1, prule2}]

parameters.name: {vars, vals}
parameters.description: Keys of the new variable and value columns.

tools.name: ColumnwiseValue
tools.description: Inside a row function used by TransformColumns/ConstructColumns, ColumnwiseValue[expr] marks a sub-expression to be evaluated once over whole columns (e.g. a column mean or maximum) rather than per row, and ColumnwiseThread[expr] evaluates it columnwise and threads the result over rows - enabling vectorized normalisation, ranking and cumulative operations within the row-function syntax.
tools.usage:
TransformColumns[tab, "share" -> (#amount/ColumnwiseValue[Total[#amount]] &)]
TransformColumns[tab, "cum" -> ColumnwiseThread[Accumulate[#amount]] &]
ConstructColumns[tab, {"z" -> ((#x - ColumnwiseValue[Mean[#x]])/ColumnwiseValue[StandardDeviation[#x]] &)}]

tools.name: MissingFallback
tools.description: MissingFallback[e1, e2, ...] returns the first argument that is not Missing - the COALESCE of Tabular row functions - used to fill gaps from alternative columns or defaults inside TransformColumns and to make aggregations robust to missing values.
tools.usage:
MissingFallback[e1, e2, ...]
TransformColumns[tab, "phone" -> (MissingFallback[#mobile, #landline, "n/a"] &)]

tools.name: Tabular indexing and querying
tools.description: Tabular objects (listed under Tabular) support Dataset-style part access and queries: tab[i] (row), tab[All, "col"] (column), tab[Select[#x > 1 &]], tab[Select[cond], {"a", "b"}], tab[SortBy[#col &]], tab[GroupBy["key"]], tab[TakeLargestBy[#v &, 5]], Length/Dimensions, Take/Drop, Join (row-wise) and JoinAcross (key-based joins), Map (row functions), and Import/Export in CSV/TSV/XLSX/Parquet/Arrow/JSON keep types. Use Tabular instead of Dataset for large typed tables.
tools.usage:
tab[i]
tab[All, "col"]
tab[Select[#price > 10 &]]
tab[Select[#region == "EU" &], {"name", "price"}]
tab[SortBy[-#price &]]
tab[GroupBy["region"]]
JoinAcross[tab1, tab2, "key"]
JoinAcross[tab1, tab2, "key", "Left"]
Export["out.parquet", tab]
